brief: A planter of four cells with a water pipe running through the bases to feed every cell.

requirements.evidence: piece:0..3,0,0 full bases, each with a hex-bin-third-drain bin filled with soil and planted (prop:1–4).

requirements.requirement: Water pipe running through the bases
requirements.evidence: run:run-1 in irrigation mode, entering the outer edge of cell 0,0 and passing through cells 1,0, 2,0 and 3,0.

The run passes straight through all four cells. In the configurator, cells on a straight run take only third-depth bins, so all four beds are shallow. The pipe end caps were added automatically: check that the inlet is left open for connecting a supply.

requirements.requirement: Watertight and suitable for soil and water (implied)
requirements.evidence: The configurator checks fit only. It cannot judge whether the printed parts are waterproof or hold up to soil and water.

finish.summary: Four full bases in a straight row (q0–3), one irrigation pipe run (run:run-1) straight through all four, and a third-depth drain bin in each cell filled with soil and planted with a cabbage seedling. Caps and joint bolts added. check_build: no rule errors, meshClash clear.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: 1 run IRRIGATION: non-potable supply. Corners are flexible hose, glued into Sch 40 sockets, one coupling wherever hose meets rigid pipe.

Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
cuts: buy 1 x 10 ft 3/4 in Sch 40 PVC pipe, OD 26.67 mm (US). Metric 25/32 mm pipe does not fit.
- fit a BACKFLOW PREVENTER at the hose bib: this system is a cross-connection without one
- fit a 25-40 psi PRESSURE REGULATOR at the inlet
- drain the system before it freezes
